Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed collision in a parking lot with reported neck pain, stiffness, and headache
consistent with cervical strain. Over the course of eleven visits, care consisted of manual therapy, guided stretching,
and a home exercise program with periodic reassessment. The mechanism of injury and the reported symptoms are
closely aligned, and the clinical picture fits the force involved in this type of impact. Range of motion was reduced in
several planes and palpation of the cervical paraspinal muscles produced tenderness, while neurological screening
and certain orthopedic provocation tests were within normal limits. The course of treatment extended somewhat
longer than is typical for a strain of this severity, reflecting a gradual rather than rapid response. No prior injury or
treatemnt involving the same region is documented in the available history. Billing records reflect each service once
as delivered, with no duplicate or repeated charges. Ongoing plan includes contniued home exercise and follow-up if
symptoms recur.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
